e9321d51f3fee066: MELAKA, Oct 17 — The Education Ministry (MOE) has left the investigation into the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Negeri Sembilan yesterday to the police.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry always adopts a vigilant approach towards the discovery of any suspicious items at schools nationwide.
“We urge all principals, headmasters and school personnel to remain vigilant and prepared, especially when it comes to matters involving school safety.
“Once again, we would like to thank the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for ensuring that all aspects of security are given priority,” she said.
She was speaking to reporters after officiating the ‘Fadhlina Membaca’ Women’s Reading Club with the Education Minister here today.
Yesterday, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that police had received nine reports concerning the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Nilai and Tampin.
Alzafny was reported as saying that inspections found all the boxes contained wheat flour and plastic plates. — Bernama
13213ecf32ed7a80: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has reached a significant milestone in the Silicon Island project, with Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow making his first vehicular visit to the island and launching the Silicon Island Experience Centre today.
He said the mega development would serve as a major catalyst for the state's economic growth over the next 50 years.
"Silicon Island is not just another reclamation project, but a strategic catalyst for the state's economic growth for the next 50 years," he said during the visit.
Chow said the project built on Penang's 50-year legacy in the semiconductor industry by introducing high-value manufacturing, research and development, and artificial intelligence capabilities.

He reaffirmed the state government's commitment to low-carbon development through the 280ha Green Tech Park and the 5-Diamond Low Carbon City Framework, while continuing to support local fishermen through financial assistance and community programmes.

Speaking at the launch, state Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the Experience Centre served as a crucial link between the master plan and its physical implementation.

He highlighted key infrastructure components, including the Pan Island Link 2A (PIL2A) bridge connecting Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island, which is designed to ensure smooth logistics and transport integration.

"The state government's commitment goes beyond building roads and bridges. Silicon Island is designed for the future, with sustainable transport, smart traffic systems, integrated pedestrian and bicycle lanes, and resilient digital infrastructure," he said.
Penang Infrastructure Corporation chief executive officer Datuk Seri Farizan Darus said the 2,500sqft facility was completed in four months at a cost of RM2.5 million.

It features an advanced LED scale model controlled via an iPad, offering interactive views of the 920ha master plan, including infrastructure networks, 160.8ha of dedicated green spaces and marine conservation zones.
Farizan said physical land reclamation at the site had reached 200ha.

Work on the RM420 million PIL2A contract was progressing smoothly, with the first phase featuring a 1.5km marine bridge scheduled to open its first section by December 2028, ahead of full completion in June 2029.
He added that more than RM30 million had been disbursed to local fishermen under the Social Impact Management Plan (SIMP), alongside ongoing ecological mitigation projects.
8204e814ecc6cd7a: TUMPAT: The elder sister of Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, told her two young nieces this morning that their mother had died, but withheld details of her death after she was found murdered at government quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA, Nilai, Negri Sembilan, on Thursday.
Marliza Ibrahim, 48, said she told the children, aged five and six, that their mother had died of an illness rather than reveal the circumstances of her death.
"When they asked why, I simply told them she was sick," she said.
"I could not bring myself to tell them the actual incident, as they are too young to understand," she said when contacted today.
Marliza added that their family home in Kampung Banjir, Telaga Lanas, continues to receive visitors, including friends of the deceased.
She said a post-mortem was conducted this morning, and the remains will be brought back to their hometown for burial at the Tanjung Islamic Cemetery in Pengkalan Kubor immediately upon arrival.
Norhazwani was a Customs Officer who transferred to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency scheme and was stationed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
It was previously reported that she was allegedly stabbed to death by her husband at their home in the KLIA quarters in Nilai.

The victim suffered two stab wounds to the left abdomen and one to the right cheek. The suspect surrendered to police shortly after the incident and has been remanded for seven days starting yesterday to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
f6313d5dbf5757f1: SINGAPORE: Ongoing fires in Indonesia that have blanketed parts of Southeast Asia with toxic haze have triggered the highest-level alert by the regional bloc's climate and fire monitor.
"Activation of Alert Level 3 for the Southern Asean region," the Singapore Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre said on its website, seen on Saturday.

Based near Singapore's Changi Airport, the ASMC uses a four-tiered alert level system, from zero to three, with the highest triggered if there is a "high risk of severe transboundary haze in the region."

This included significant and persistent hotspot activities with widespread moderate to dense smoke haze, observed over two or more consecutive days, dry weather persisting and wind continuing to blow haze towards neighbouring Asean countries.
The ASMC alert was issued Friday, but similar alerts have already been handed out twice this year – on Aug 26 and March 27.
The months-long spell of haze has been disrupting life in large parts of Southeast Asia, closing schools and spiking respiratory complaints.
Singapore said on Friday it would issue warnings to seven companies in Indonesia it identified as responsible for fires but warned the worst may yet to come.
f27052a8aa92bc05: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The public has been reminded not to use a child’s ‘nasab’ (birth or lineage) status as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against them, forcing them to bear a social burden throughout their lives.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a child should not be blamed for the circumstances of their birth, as Islamic principles clearly state that no individual bears the sins of another.
He said that while legal rulings concerning lineage must be upheld, they should not be used as an excuse to subject children to social judgement.
“Discussions on legal rulings should not be used as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against a child.

“We need to build a society that can distinguish between evaluating an act and condemning a person for the rest of their life,” he said when delivering his speech at the ‘Seminar Nasab Kebangsaan: Dinamika Cabaran Keluarga Kosmopolitan (SANAD) 2026’, organised by Persatuan Kebajikan Bayt Al-Rahmah, here today.
Zulkifli said society should also be mindful of the language used within families, educational institutions and administrative settings to avoid causing children to bear a prolonged social stigma.
He said the Quranic principle that no individual bears the sins of another should serve as a moral foundation for ensuring that children are not blamed for the circumstances of their birth.

At the same time, Zulkifli said due attention should be given to mothers facing pregnancy or childbirth crises, as they might need assistance in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education and rebuilding their emotional stability.

“They may need support in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education, rebuilding their emotional stability, improving family relationships or planning their future more systematically,” he said.

On the matter of lineage, Zulkifli said it should not be addressed based solely on assumptions, public perceptions or emotions, but required careful examination of the facts, an understanding of syariah principles and consultation with the relevant authorities.

He said the issue also had implications for family matters, inheritance, guardianship, mahram relationships, as well as the naming and registration of births, all of which needed to be examined in accordance with the relevant religious rulings and legal provisions.

He said the management of lineage-related issues should not stop at determining the legal status alone, as attention must also be given to the child’s care, education, protection, well-being and future.

In this regard, he stressed the importance of integrated cooperation among religious institutions, courts, government agencies, welfare organisations, counselling service providers and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in addressing challenges related to lineage.

“Lineage issues cannot be understood from just one perspective. They require scholarly examination, an understanding of syariah principles, accuracy in legal and administrative matters, as well as concern for the impact on individuals and families,” he said.
Zulkifli said NGOs and shelters also played an important role in identifying gaps in support and unmet needs among mothers and children. — Bernama
e71b1524b9229e1b: KUALA LUMPUR: Over three years after losing his sight, actor and director Muhammad Iqbal Mazlan is still fighting to rebuild his career in the creative industry.
But finding work in his field is no longer as easy as it once was.
Iqbal, 37, won the first season of the acting talent show Pilih Kasih in 2009.
He previously starred in various TV dramas, telemovies, and theatre productions. He even worked alongside renowned director Erma Fatima.
But his life changed completely in March 2023 when he lost his sight to Frosted branch angiitis—a condition he explained was caused by a Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection.

"I was actually quite healthy with no symptoms. But on the night before it happened, I felt extremely fatigued and experienced severe eye strain while finishing a documentary script, so I took a brief rest.
"When I woke up, my world was in complete darkness. It was hard to imagine life after that because the gift I used to earn a living was suddenly gone," he told Bernama.
It took Iqbal over a year to pick himself back up.
During that time, he received treatment for eye inflammation and suffered complications from fluid in his lungs, which he attributed to the side effects of his medication.
An even bigger hurdle awaited him when he tried to return to work.
As expected, several production companies he had previously worked with went quiet when he offered his services as a director, presenter, and voiceover artiste.
"Many production houses that had collaborated with me and praised my work suddenly went quiet when I fell ill. What hurt most was when industry peers started drifting away.
"One rejection particularly stands out where they told me point-blank, 'We don't have any confidence in you.' The rest just offered silence," he recalled.
To make ends meet, he currently runs a food stall with a friend selling buttermilk chicken and gulai kawah in Shah Alam.
His chance to return to his passion came when production company Art Ornament Sdn Bhd trusted him to direct the film Jay (Buka Langkah) in June 2024. The movie is set for release in January 2027.
Iqbal explained that losing his sight does not stop him from visualising scenes or giving clear directions to his camera team.

"Even though I cannot see, I must have a clear visual concept to bring the script to life, imagining it as if I were watching a movie in a cinema. I lay out the detailed visuals and shots I want to achieve to the camera operator.
"For instance, I specify the exact direction an actor should step from, along with the accompanying ambient sounds. If a director lacks visualisation, the work becomes bland," he explained.
The film's producer and co-director, Aida Othman, said Iqbal got the job based purely on his talent, with a crew helping him handle technical tasks on set.

"We should not view them through the lens of their disability, but rather by what they are capable of achieving. Iqbal's strength lies in his exceptionally clear explanation of character, emotion, and the message he wants to convey to the audience. We chose to give him this chance because we believe in his talent," she said.
Iqbal's story shows that visually impaired individuals can create great work when given the right support.
But such opportunities remain rare in the creative sector.

According to figures from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) between 2020 and 2026, only five visually impaired people secured jobs in the arts, entertainment, and recreation sector out of 716 total placements—just 0.7 per cent.
Although the figures are low, the data does not reveal the precise reasons for the poor placement rate.
The Social Welfare Department (JKM) reported that as of July this year, 70,135 visually impaired individuals were registered nationwide, including 37,616 aged between 16 and 60.
Musician and music arranger Lui Chee Chau, 46, faces a similar struggle.
Despite holding formal qualifications and having over a decade of industry experience, he is still searching for full-time work.
Lui began his career as a music arranger and sound engineer at a studio in Kuala Lumpur in 2003.
After the studio closed, he worked full-time for 14 years at a ringtone company.
Finding work became difficult around 2016 after he applied for sound engineering jobs and went to interviews without telling potential employers beforehand about his sight loss.
"He told me my work was good. But to make things easier for me, he said he would call if any work could be done from home," Lui recalled.
Lui later applied for three other music jobs, but only one led to an interview before he was passed over.
Although no employer explicitly said his sight loss was the reason he was turned down, the experience raises questions about how much prejudice still affects job prospects for disabled people.
"I feel that is one of the main limitations—when people restrict our choices based on assumptions without evaluating our actual capabilities," he said.
Lui now teaches piano and drums part-time, as well as running weekly music lessons at a local church.

349f94d602764dae: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 17 — Local fast-food chain Marrybrown aims to open 30 new outlets nationwide by 2027 as part of its strategy to expand operations and strengthen its position in the fast-food industry.
Marrybrown Malaysia chief executive officer Daniel Chan Lek Seong said the plan aligns with the company’s efforts to continue expanding its business network to meet domestic demand.

“Marrybrown now has around 300 outlets in Malaysia, with Johor recording the highest number at around 100 outlets since the brand originated from that state,” he told Bernama after attending the launch of the Road to Francaise International Malaysia 2027 (FIM2027) programme here yesterday.

Chan said the company also plans to expand its network in Johor in line with the state’s economic development, including the development of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link project.
On international developments, Daniel said Marrybrown, which currently has around 500 outlets in 16 countries, including Malaysia, is also exploring new markets, including Cambodia and Egypt.
He said the first outlet in Cambodia is scheduled to open this November, with renovations currently underway.
Chan said his company aims to continue expanding its international presence by exploring three to five new country markets each year, subject to identified business opportunities.

He said the effort was also carried out in collaboration with various parties, including related agencies and the Malaysian Franchise Association (MFA), to strengthen the position of local brands in the global market.
Meanwhile, Daniel said about 90 per cent of Marrybrown’s raw materials come from local suppliers, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), to support the domestic supply chain.
He added that the company is also currently maintaining menu prices and prioritising affordability for consumers. — Bernama
7346bf1c3b3ada38: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah tomorrow.
Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) said the decision follows a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment after temporary suspensions triggered by security concerns in Saudi Arabia.

"Passengers travelling to and from both destinations from Oct 18 should verify their flight schedules and ensure their contact details are updated through the 'My Booking' section on its website or mobile app.
"Passengers who booked through third-party platforms or travel agents should contact their respective providers directly to confirm their travel arrangements.
"For assistance, passengers can use the airline's Live Chat service or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 within Malaysia or +603 7843 3000 from overseas," it said in a statement.
The airline also said that it would continue to monitor developments in the region as the safety and security of its passengers and crew remain its highest priority.

It was reported that Malaysia Airlines had cancelled flights between Kuala Lumpur and Jeddah and Madinah from Oct 12 to 17 following reported Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport.
0c7d568291b3abb3: LAS VEGAS: American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit for Saturday's fight against Tomoki Kameda of Japan, organisers said on Friday.
Kameda, 35, will be able to clinch the vacant title if he wins the fight, which will go ahead as scheduled in Las Vegas.
"Honestly, it's disrespectful, because I'm here, I suffered too. I did my thing. I'm ready for tomorrow," Kameda said, speaking via a translator.
"It has been 18 months since I fought, but look at me, look how shredded I am. You know I'm ready. Everything remains the same, I'm going for the title tomorrow."
Figueroa, 29, clinched the featherweight title in February after beating Briton Nick Ball in Liverpool.
If he wins the fight against Kameda, the title will remain vacant. - Reuters
29096b20edcb41c7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Free fashion shipping, AI-powered virtual fitting rooms and more than 1,400 local return points — Taobao is pulling out the stops for Malaysian shoppers ahead of its annual 11.11 Global Shopping Festival.

The online shopping platform has unveiled a raft of upgrades designed to make cross-border shopping less of a gamble, particularly when it comes to finding the right outfit, comparing products and returning purchases that don't quite live up to expectations.

Running from October 20 at 8pm until November 13, this year's shopping extravaganza promises access to more than three billion products, spanning fashion, homeware, furniture, collectibles, beauty and lifestyle essentials.

And for shoppers who have ever hesitated over an international order because of shipping fees or the hassle of returns, Taobao is hoping its latest changes will make hitting the checkout button a little easier.
Free shipping, even if you're buying just one item
One of the biggest draws this year is free shipping across Taobao's fashion category, with no minimum spending requirement.
That means shoppers can pick up a single item without having to pad their baskets just to qualify for free delivery.

According to Taobao Malaysia, more than 400 million products are available with free shipping, with the offer extending to selected categories including home and living, tableware, toys, pet accessories, beauty tools and travel essentials.
For those who want their purchases sooner rather than later, eligible orders can also be upgraded to air shipping, with delivery taking as little as five days in key cities.
Other deals include discounts of up to 15 per cent across the platform, daily air shipping vouchers released at noon and 8pm, and instant rebates of up to RM50 for eligible RHB Bank cardholders.
New users can enjoy perks worth up to RM40, while shoppers using Taobao's English-language app can access exclusive platform vouchers offering discounts of up to 50 per cent.
Your next fitting room could be powered by AI
Buying clothes online can be a hit-or-miss affair, especially when the model looks great in an outfit but you're not entirely convinced it will work for you.
Taobao is tackling that uncertainty with AI Try-On, a feature that allows shoppers to upload their own photographs and visualise how fashion items might look on them before making a purchase.
It's one of four AI-powered features the platform is introducing to make navigating its enormous catalogue less overwhelming.
An AI Shopping Assistant offers personalised recommendations based on shoppers' needs, alongside real-time price comparisons and product quality assessments.
Meanwhile, AI Product Insights helps shoppers cut through lengthy product descriptions and customer reviews by highlighting key features, translating specifications and summarising the pros and cons.
There's also Voice-Search-by-Hold, which allows users to describe what they're looking for rather than having to figure out the perfect search term.
Together, the tools are designed to make product discovery more intuitive, particularly for shoppers who know what they want but aren't quite sure how to find it.
Returning purchases is about to get easier
Perhaps the biggest practical change, however, is happening after checkout.
Starting in November, Taobao will progressively introduce more than 1,400 local return drop-off points across Malaysia through a collaboration with J&T Express.
The arrangement will allow customers to return eligible purchases at participating locations without having to organise international shipping themselves.
It's a move aimed at addressing one of the longstanding frustrations of cross-border shopping: what happens when something arrives damaged, doesn't fit or simply isn't what you expected?
The expanded returns network complements Taobao Official Logistics, which offers shipping information, customer support and compensation protection for eligible lost or damaged shipments.
Taobao Malaysia country head Jess Lew said consumers were increasingly looking for products that matched their interests and lifestyles, rather than simply shopping for everyday necessities.

"Today's consumers are looking beyond basic necessities. They are seeking products that reflect their interests, lifestyles and aspirations. At Taobao, our goal is not only to bring Malaysians access to Everything and Anything, but also to make the experience of discovering and purchasing these products as seamless as possible."
She said the company had spent years adapting its services to Malaysian consumers through language support, payment partnerships and logistics improvements.
"The expansion of our local return network is another important step towards giving consumers greater confidence and convenience when shopping across borders," she added.
Thinking bigger? Sofas and furniture are in the mix too
It's not just fashion getting an upgrade.
Taobao is also targeting Malaysians looking to spruce up their homes, with more than one million furniture products now eligible for direct shipping to Malaysia.
The selection includes sofas, dining tables and height-adjustable desks, potentially opening up more options for shoppers furnishing a new home or giving an existing space a makeover.
During the 11.11 campaign, eligible furniture purchases can also enjoy shipping vouchers worth up to RM30.
The platform said its official logistics service also provides compensation protection for eligible damaged items, offering some reassurance to consumers considering larger purchases.
And there's something for Zhang Linghe fans
Taobao is also taking its 11.11 celebrations offline, with a little star power courtesy of Chinese actor Zhang Linghe.
Following its recently announced partnership with the actor, the platform has introduced a Zhang Linghe-themed app interface and a daily treasure hunt campaign.
Fans will also have opportunities to get their hands on exclusive merchandise at special activations in Malaysia.
The first will take place at LaLaport Kuala Lumpur on October 24 and 25, followed by another at Xiamen University Malaysia on October 27 and 28.
Both events will feature interactive experiences and opportunities to redeem Zhang Linghe merchandise.
With free fashion shipping, AI-assisted shopping and an expanded returns network, Taobao is pitching this year's 11.11 festival as more than another round of discounts.
For Malaysian shoppers, the real attraction may be a simpler online shopping experience — from discovering the perfect purchase to sending it back when things don't quite work out.
b41a2609779af39f: KOTA MARUDU, Oct 17 — A woman on her way to send her son to school was killed when the motorcycle she was riding was involved in an accident at the Kampung Marak Parak junction, here, early yesterday.
Liza Jius, 34, died at the scene from severe head injuries, while her seven-year-old son, who was riding pillion and attends Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Marak Parak, sustained minor injuries.
District Police Chief Supt Simiun Lomudin said the accident occurred at about 6.19am and involved the Modenas Kriss and a Toyota Hilux driven by a 40-year-old man.
“The Hilux driver was believed to have been overtaking the motorcycle in front of him when it turned right to enter the school junction, resulting in a collision,” he said.
Investigations were ongoing under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
In TAWAU, a 19-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a collision involving a Perodua Axia at Batu 3, Jalan Apas, at about 12.30pm yesterday.
District Fire and Rescue Station Chief Deputy Superintendent of Fire and Rescue II Jemishin Ujin said Mohd Adrian was pronounced dead at the scene.
“The car’s 31-year-old female driver and 40-year-old female front passenger sustained minor injuries in the accident,” he told Daily Express.

Jemishin said the front passenger was trapped in the vehicle before firefighters rescued her using hydraulic cutting equipment and handed her over to Health Ministry personnel for further treatment. — Daily Express

b7985423cb4ec692: KUALA LUMPUR: The Starting Basic Salary Guidelines based on the Malaysia Standard Classification of Occupations (Masco) must be supported by transparent monitoring and reporting mechanisms to ensure employer compliance, an economic analyst said.

Putra Business School Associate Professor Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said that without clear enforcement mechanisms, employers could disregard the guidelines without legal consequences, leaving graduates unable to challenge low salary offers.
He said setting a starting salary of RM2,500 would not guarantee equity unless job duties, skill levels, and responsibilities were accurately assessed.
"Job classifications under Masco must be reviewed based on actual duties, not merely job titles stated in employment contracts.
"The government must also clearly define basic salary and allowances to prevent employers from including bonuses, overtime, or variable payments to obscure actual salary rates," he said.

He was commenting on the Human Resources Ministry's plan to draft guidelines for minimum wage policies and starting basic salaries for graduates and semi-skilled workers, as announced in the 2027 Budget.

Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the guidelines would provide a reference for starting basic salaries by job category and qualification level, while amendments to the National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011 (Act 732) were being fine-tuned to make minimum wage mandatory for graduates.
Razman said pending the amendments, the government should establish a clear transition plan with annual compliance targets, salary rate reporting, and public disclosures of sector compliance levels.
He added that government-linked companies and government contractors should lead by example, with incentives such as procurement priority offered to compliant employers.
To ensure effective implementation, he recommended risk-based compliance audits, confidential complaint channels, and whistleblower protection.

On the e-Wages mechanism being fine-tuned by the ministry, Razman suggested integrating salary data with bank transactions, employment contracts, payslips, Employees Provident Fund, Social Security Organisation and tax records.
He said this would allow the government to cross-check promised salaries against actual payments, detecting late payments or underpayments.

"Automated risk analysis could help the Labour Department target inspections at high-risk employers. However, the system must have data security safeguards and verification procedures before enforcement action is taken," he said.

Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Sabah branch senior lecturer Dr Jain Yassin said the government should provide transparent salary data by occupation, qualifications, sector, and location to help graduates evaluate job offers accurately.
"To address information gaps, the government could enhance the e-Masco portal by providing regularly updated salary information by occupation, qualifications, and skill levels," he said.

Jain added that the e-Wages mechanism should serve as an early warning system integrated with artificial intelligence (AI), payroll data, and labour market analysis to detect non-compliance systematically.
He also proposed appointing independent monitors, including professional bodies, university researchers, or labour economists, to conduct regular audits.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget on Oct 9, announced that the government agreed to raise the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027, benefiting over four million workers.
70002717ae0a8d60: KOTA TINGGI: The second phase of the Johor Elephant Sanctuary (JES) upgrade project is 82 per cent complete and is scheduled for full completion in the first quarter of 2027.

State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the project, worth more than RM11 million, included the construction of new facilities to improve visitor comfort and ensure more systematic wildlife conservation management.
He said the new facilities included a visitor hall, security room, observation deck and a dedicated platform for viewing elephants.
"The opening of the sanctuary will allow the public to observe the elephants' daily routines up close in a safe and controlled environment.
"Elephants are among Johor's natural treasures that we must protect. Following several recent incidents of human-elephant conflict, efforts to conserve and protect wild elephants must continue.
"I hope JES will help the public learn more about the lives of elephants and understand the importance of protecting wildlife and maintaining environmental balance," he said in a statement yesterday.

He said the new phase was expected to further enhance JES's potential as an environmental education centre and a major ecotourism attraction in the state, while strengthening Johor's ongoing efforts to address human-elephant conflict.
Ling made a working visit to JES yesterday to inspect progress on the second phase of the sanctuary's upgrade project.
00e81274e488a02d: PETALING JAYA, Oct 17 — The Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre (JCPAC) offers Malaysian artistes opportunities to develop their talents through world-class facilities and collaboration with international artistes.

Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah said the centre, developed with an investment of more than RM200 million at Sunway Square here, aims to serve as a platform for artistes to pursue meaningful careers and contribute to the growth of the creative economy.
“Our investment in JCPAC reflects our belief that excellence in the performing arts deserves the same commitment, resources and opportunities that we devote to education and research.

“I firmly believe that Malaysian artistes deserve the opportunity to learn and develop their craft on the finest stages. With the right support, facilities and encouragement, there’s no limit to what they can achieve,” he said in his keynote address at JCPAC’s launch last night.

The launch featured Brand New Day: A Symphonic Broadway Celebration, with 22 singers, eight dancers and the 73-piece TUTAN Festival Orchestra directed by Kevin Field, performing songs from Les Misérables, The Phantom of the Opera, Miss Saigon, Wicked and Dreamgirls.

Cheah hoped JCPAC would cultivate strong relationships with renowned performing arts organisations around the world, providing opportunities for local artistes and creative professionals to learn, exchange ideas and broaden their horizons.
“We have much to contribute to the global cultural landscape and our artistes deserve every opportunity to be seen, heard and appreciated beyond our shores,” he said.

He added that JCPAC’s success will not be measured simply by the number of performances it hosts, but by the opportunities it creates for young people to discover their gifts, artistes to grow in their chosen path and communities to come together and enjoy the arts.

He said the idea of establishing JCPAC, which forms part of the RM1.8 billion Sunway Square integrated development, was first explored in 2018 to enrich the educational experience at Sunway University while serving the wider Sunway City community.
According to Cheah, a holistic approach to education should place equal emphasis on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), as well as the arts and humanities.

“Technology may transform the way we live and work, but it can never replace the wisdom and human connection that the arts inspire. The arts and culture must remain at the heart of our educational ecosystem, which I believe no technology and AI can replace,” he said.

On JCPAC’s development, Cheah said its design drew inspiration from the tin mining landscape on which Sunway City was built, with some RM30 million dedicated to its sound system and acoustic technology.

The 1,200-seat Grand Theatre features Malaysia’s first combined installation of L-Acoustics L-ISA immersive sound and Ambiance active acoustics, allowing the theatre’s acoustics to be adapted for orchestral music, musical theatre and spoken drama without physically altering its architecture.
The centre also houses The Studio, which accommodates up to 150 people and has a portable stage and reconfigurable seating for smaller performances, experimental work and educational programmes.

Sharing his personal connection with music, Cheah recalled playing the drums in The Ambassadors, a band he formed with fellow Malaysian students in Melbourne, Australia, in the 1960s, which once backed a young Olivia Newton-John at St Kilda Town Hall.
“And although I eventually pursued a career in business instead of music, those years left me with a lifelong appreciation for the arts,” he said.

Upcoming productions at JCPAC include Puteri Gunung Ledang The Musical from October 31, Dama Asia’s The Butterfly Lovers The Musical in November, and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory The Musical from December 22 to January 10, 2027. — Bernama

e5dfeb6a199309d2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Immigration Department detained 190 foreigners and two local men during a raid on an entertainment centre in Pudu here early today following public complaints about disturbances.
Its Enforcement Division director, Datuk Basri Othman, said those detained comprised 99 men and 91 women, aged between 20 and 41.
Of the foreigners, 188 were Indonesians, while the other two were from Bangladesh and India.
The two local men are believed to be the employer and caretaker of the entertainment centre, which is located about 10 metres from a mosque.

“Several rooms in the premises were used for entertainment, with between 50 and 60 people in each room at the time of the raid. Immigration offences detected included overstaying and not possessing valid travel documents,” he told reporters after the operation.
All those detained were taken to an immigration depot for investigation under Sections 6(1)(c) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
During the raid, Bernama observed white powder suspected to be drugs on several plates, as well as condoms in the rooms.
Basri said further investigations would be conducted into the possibility of immoral activities at the premises. — Bernama
5b9e6b11be1ea821: LYON, Oct 17 — Oscar-winning filmmaker brothers Ethan and Joel Coen told AFP they plan to make another movie together, having taken a break from their joint directing work that produced a string of classics from Fargo to Barton Fink.
Both of them have latterly turned to personal projects, working with their wives — film editor Tricia Cooke and actress Frances McDormand — on movies such as Honey Don’t and The Tragedy of Macbeth.
But they said they planned to reunite soon behind the camera, joking that it had to come soon because of their advancing ages.

“We’re getting old. It better be the near future,” Joel, 71, told AFP in a joint interview ahead of a prize ceremony in the French city of Lyon where they are being given the “Lumiere” lifetime achievement award.

“We have a number of different things in what we call the library, things that we’ve written before,” he added. “And then other things that we’ve thought about writing scripts about and never gotten around. So we don’t know yet.”
He denied reports that “there’s some kind of schism, that there’s some kind of break that happened. In fact, it’s not anything like that.”

Their last film together was 2018’s The Ballad of Buster Scruggs, an offbeat Oscar-nominated Western starring Tim Blake Nelson, which followed the 1950s Hollywood-set satirical comedy Hail, Caesar! in 2016.

Joel will release another solo project next year called Jack of Spades with Josh O’Connor, while Ethan has done a documentary about American pianist Jerry Lee Lewis as well as two other films with lesbian heroines.
The brothers declined to give any details about what their next joint project would be, but it is unlikely to be fantasy-based.

“It’s definitely some weird cultural thing where mainstream movies are now mostly fantasy: fantasy, science fiction, horror, comic books, all different kinds of fantasy,” Ethan, 69, explained. “It’s a sad thing for us because we’ve never been drawn to those kinds of things.”
He also ruled out doing a TV series, despite serving as an executive producer on the long-running Fargo television adaptation.
“You have to sort of understand that structure in order to do it successfully. And it’s just not what we do. It’s not the way our brains think about stories,” Joel explained. — AFP
f03f38277deb67a6: GEORGE TOWN: Transport Minister Anthony Loke has rejected calls to ban foreigners from Rapid KL buses, saying passengers who cause disturbances or behave indecently can face enforcement action.
He said auxiliary police could intervene against unruly passengers, while bus drivers could take appropriate action and refer offenders to the police when necessary.
"We are not an isolated country. How can we prohibit foreigners from taking the bus? That is an impossible proposal," he told reporters after launching Penang's first electric bus here today.

Loke was responding to complaints from Rapid KL commuters about alleged misconduct by some foreign passengers, including the misuse of public transport facilities, trespassing and behaviour that had left other passengers uncomfortable.

The issue has also sparked debate on social media following a Threads post alleging that a foreign child urinated on the ground before boarding a Rapid KL bus, after which the child's mother sat on the bus floor to change the child's clothes.
The account claimed other passengers wanted the driver to ask the pair to leave but alleged that the driver did not intervene.

Some commuters have called for Rapid KL to empower drivers to refuse boarding or ask passengers to disembark if they behave in an unruly or disrespectful manner, including children accompanied by their parents.
Loke said foreigners could not be barred from public transport as a group, but stressed that individual misconduct could warrant enforcement action.
He said passengers who behaved indecently or disturbed others could be detained where necessary and referred to the police.
5ad8a8367fbc2867: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flight operations to and from Jeddah and Madinah, Saudi Arabia, effective tomorrow (October 18) following a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment.

The national carrier advised passengers travelling to or from the two destinations to check their flight schedules and ensure their contact details are updated via the “My Booking” feature on its website or mobile application.

“Passengers who made their bookings through third-party platforms or travel agents are advised to contact their respective booking providers directly regarding their travel arrangements,” it said in a statement today.

Malaysia Airlines said customers requiring assistance could use the Live Chat feature on its website or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 (within Malaysia) or +603 7843 3000 (international).
The airline also thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the temporary suspension of flights to the two destinations.
It said it would continue to closely monitor developments in the region, with the safety and security of passengers and crew remaining its highest priority. — Bernama
c33f7a6a9fc46336: KUALA TERENGGANU: Seorang pesara kerajaan kerugian sebanyak RM42,580 selepas diperdaya sindiket skim gandaan wang dalam talian yang tidak wujud.
Ketua Polis Kuala Terengganu, Azli Mohd Noor, berkata pada 7 Okt lalu mangsa wanita berusia 71 tahun melihat iklan skim menggandakan wang menerusi laman Facebook.
Beliau berkata, mangsa yang berminat telah menghubungi suspek dikenali sebagai ‘ustaz Hilmi Firdausi’ melalui WhatsApp.
"Mangsa yang terperdaya telah membuat lima kali bayaran berjumlah RM42,580 menggunakan wang simpanan dan dijanjikan pulangan sebanyak RM300,000.
"Bagaimanapun, setelah membuat pembayaran tersebut, suspek meminta mangsa membuat tambahan sebanyak RM50,000 untuk mendapatkan keuntungan," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Azli berkata, mangsa yang curiga enggan mengikuti arahan dan membuat laporan polis pada 11.06 malam, Khamis lalu.
Beliau berkata, kes disiasat mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan.
f48e5b1f1ec7fd9d: WASHINGTON: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public on Friday.

Temu faces several lawsuits from US states concerned that the company unlawfully harvests US user data that could be accessed by the Chinese government. Texas is the first to resolve such claims. It is also the first time the company has agreed to keep personal data on US servers and restrict when it can be sent to China, Texas officials said.

The company agreed to conduct annual independent product safety testing to identify products containing dangerous chemicals and materials. Temu must remove any products found to contain dangerous materials, terminate the seller and its affiliated stores, notify affected Texas consumers and issue full refunds.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said the settlement also requires Temu "to implement rigorous new product audits and safety standards to protect consumers from dangerous materials in products, including clothing and children’s items."
He added it will prevent Temu from collecting and using Americans' data.
Temu had more than 82.4 million active users in the US as of September 2023, Paxton's office said.

Temu will pay US$3 million to the state as part of the settlement and Texas said failure to abide by various data security provisions would result in a potential US$8 million penalty each year a violation occurs.
Several states sued Temu in the wake of reports alleging Temu and parent company PDD ‌Holdings used invasive mechanisms in their apps.

Temu, which did not admit wrongdoing, said in a statement the company "has come to an agreement to resolve this matter as we continue to focus on serving consumers and supporting businesses across Texas."
Under the terms of the settlement, Temu agreed to restrict access to US data necessary to fulfill a transaction, such as shipping addresses, to China.
Texas alleged that Temu used code that allows an inappropriate level of access to users’ devices. Temu has denied the allegations.
05e8e07d6d7ecec9: SHAH ALAM: Twin sisters never expected their university journey at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to culminate in such a proud achievement, with both receiving the UiTM 2026 Best Graduate Award at the university's 105th Convocation Ceremony today.

Making the occasion even more special, Puteri Sofea Nabeela Haris and her younger sister, Puteri Sofea Nabeeha, 24, graduates of the Faculty of Computer and Mathematical Sciences (FSKM), were proud to receive the awards from UiTM Chancellor His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, himself.

The Kuala Lumpur-born twins, who graduated with a Bachelor of Statistics, described their achievement as the result of consistent effort throughout their studies, as well as their parents' prayers and support and the assistance of lecturers, friends and the university.

For the non-identical twins, the opportunity to pursue their academic journey together was a privilege, made even more special by being able to celebrate their respective highest achievements at the same convocation ceremony.

Sharing their study techniques, Puteri Sofea Nabeela said studying together and exchanging ideas were among their strategies for understanding subjects, completing assignments and preparing for tests.

They also worked to maintain a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of at least 3.7 every semester, starting from their diploma studies, while ensuring that no important topics, particularly core subjects, were left out.

"We would brainstorm together for assignments and tests. Whenever we encountered difficult topics, we would seek help from our lecturers," she told Bernama after receiving the award at Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM, today.

Beyond their academic commitments, Puteri Sofea Nabeela said they were also active in faculty clubs and university-level activities, including corporate social responsibility (CSR) programmes, volunteer work and organising initiatives that benefited the community.
Asked whether they planned to pursue postgraduate studies, the twins said they wanted to focus on and adapt to their respective careers first.

Puteri Sofea Nabeela, the third of five siblings, is currently working at a prominent local audit firm in the field of automation using artificial intelligence (AI) technology to reduce manual processes.
Her younger sister, meanwhile, has joined a technology company as a software engineer and is involved in projects that use AI-based solutions.

At the ceremony, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim conferred the title of Professor Emeritus on Datuk Dr Roziah Mohd Janor, UiTM's first female vice-chancellor, and presented the UiTM 2026 Best Graduate Award to 15 of the university's top graduates.
Also in attendance was Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who is also UiTM Pro-Chancellor.

The ceremony, which was also attended by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir and UiTM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin, marked the start of the presentation of diplomas and degrees in various fields to 32,630 graduates, with the convocation running until Dec 16.
0fa8a559a97ba3d6: IPOH, Oct 17 — A 31-year-old motorist escaped unhurt after a tree branch fell onto his Perodua Myvi in front of the Kuala Kangsar Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) office this morning.

Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 8.57am, prompting seven personnel from the Kuala Kangsar Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene.
The driver had managed to get out of the vehicle before the firemen arrived.

Preliminary investigations found that a branch from a tree believed to be more than 50 years old had become brittle and fallen onto the car. No heavy rain or storm was reported at the time of the incident.
Sabarodzi said firefighters used a chainsaw to remove the fallen branch, and the operation ended at 9.20am. — Bernama
d07db39a6825ff73: NEW YORK, Oct 17 — Disgraced music producer Sean “Diddy” Combs, who was sentenced for prostitution-related crimes, has been transferred to a new US prison following media reports detailing an alleged brawl and special treatment behind bars.
The 56-year-old was moved from the Fort Dix lockup in New Jersey to Allenwood Low in neighbouring Pennsylvania, a Bureau of Prisons spokeswoman told AFP yesterday.
Both are low-security federal prisons for male offenders, but Allenwood Low has a population of around 1,000 compared to roughly 4,000 at Fort Dix.
US media has reported that Combs was treated at a hospital for a head injury following a fight with another prisoner last weekend.
And in September, NBC News reported that Combs enjoyed a relatively lavish lifestyle at Fort Dix, with access to contraband cellphones and liquor.
The outlet also said Combs had men cooking and cleaning for him, as well as someone to give him Chinese-style massages.
The Bureau of Prisons did not explain why Combs was transferred to the new prison.
“For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, including reasons for transfer,” a spokeswoman said.

Combs was sentenced in 2025 after a salacious trial that detailed the alleged “freak-offs” he organized: sexual marathons involving hired male escorts and his ex-girlfriend Casandra Ventura and another unidentified women.
He was acquitted by a jury of the most serious charges against him — sex trafficking and racketeering — but convicted of two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution.
Combs is due to be released from prison in March 2028. — AFP

0772a92859aa88d7: GEORGE TOWN: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd has begun rolling out its electric vehicle (EV) bus service in stages, starting with Rapid Penang today.
Transport minister Loke Siew Fook said 250 electric buses would be procured under the first phase, with 175 allocated to Rapid KL and the remaining 75 to Rapid Penang.
Of the 250 buses, 150 will be deployed under the first phase, with the remaining 100 to be introduced under the second phase.
As of Oct 13, Rapid Bus had received 52 EV buses for the first phase of rollout, with 37 units given to Rapid KL and the remaining 15 handed to Rapid Penang.
Rapid Bus is expected to receive all the buses by March next year.
“This marks a new era for Penang’s public transport system, with buses that are more environmentally friendly and quieter,” Loke said at the launch of the EV bus fleet at the Rapid Penang depot here.
Loke said the buses’ quieter operation, compared with conventional diesel-powered vehicles, might result in pedestrians and other road users not noticing them approaching.
He urged the state government and local authorities to take this into account when planning traffic management and pedestrian walkways, particularly in areas with heavy foot traffic.
The introduction of the electric buses is part of Prasarana Malaysia Bhd’s plan to procure 1,600 EV buses in stages from this year until 2031 to replace its diesel-powered fleet.
Rapid Bus will introduce two types of electric buses, measuring 12m and 8.25m in length, to cater to different traffic conditions and passenger capacity requirements.
f2c1197aa53a8390: TEHERAN: Iran on Friday denied having anything to do with attacks by Yemen's Houthis, a day after Saudi Arabia accused it of having encouraged the group's recent escalation against the kingdom.

Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.

A Saudi-led military coalition has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government for more than a decade, and reported on Friday having intercepted more missiles and drones as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from the Houthis.
A day earlier, a Saudi foreign ministry official said Iran had "encouraged" the escalation, which Tehran denied.
"The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations," Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement.

"Yemen's armed forces act according to their own interests and assessments, and such claims are not credible to those familiar with relations between Iran and its friends. Nevertheless, Iran does not consider an escalation of tensions to be in the interests of any party," he added.
The Saudi official, deputy minister for public diplomacy Dr. Rayed Krimly, had said the Houthis rejected an offer to meet in Oman at the outset of the latest round of hostilities.
Baqaei however reiterated an offer to mediate between the two sides, saying Tehran "has always been ready to use its good offices to help end the hostilities."
On Friday, a spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition said it had "intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh... and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea."
He added that "in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu", a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.

The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic government-held territory along the Red Sea coast overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.

The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.
AIRPORT STRUCK
Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.

On Friday, the local security office in Aden, the government's interim capital, said two missiles landed within the perimeter of the city's airport, "in the second incident of its kind in less than a week", adding that no one was killed.
The Houthis, in a statement attributed to a military source, said the attack targeted "the Saudi forces' command headquarters" as well as a weapons depot.
The Yemeni information ministry said in a statement that a Yemenia Airways flight from Aden to Cairo narrowly missed being struck.

It was "preparing for takeoff at the very moment when the terrorist Houthi militia targeted the airport with two missiles that landed approximately 500 metres from the aircraft and about 100 metres from the centre of the runway," a statement said.

"What occurred was not merely an assault on a civilian airport, but a direct threat to the lives of passengers and flight crews, to aviation safety, and a grave violation of international laws and norms."
The day before, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the "cowardly" act on X, calling it a "continuation of (the Houthis') criminal pattern."
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that the Houthis hit command centres for Yemeni and Saudi coalition forces housed at the palace complex.
Media affiliated with the Houthis said the attack had targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden."

4fb18cb2933e95a3: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The government cannot stop foreigners from using public buses, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said today when asked about complaints of unruly behaviour by foreigners on buses.
“We cannot stop foreigners from taking public buses,” he said.
“Public buses are public transport and everyone has the right to use them,” Loke said at a press conference after launching Rapid Penang’s electric buses at the depot in Weld Quay here.
However, Loke said all passengers, regardless of nationality, must comply with the rules and behave appropriately.
He said complaints about unruly behaviour should be reported to the bus operator or the relevant authorities, which could then take action based on the circumstances.

Complaints about foreigners behaving disruptively on public buses have previously surfaced on social media and in local news reports, including allegations of loud conversations, blocking aisles, failing to queue and refusing to follow instructions from bus staff.
Such complaints have also prompted calls for passengers to respect other commuters, keep noise levels down, avoid obstructing entrances and exits, and comply with safety instructions.
Meanwhile, Loke cautioned that the introduction of quieter electric buses must be accompanied by greater public awareness to protect pedestrians.
“We will see newer buses that are more environmentally friendly and quieter. But there is also a risk, because when they pass, many people do not realise a bus is passing,” he said.
He called on the authorities to account for the change as the state gradually renews its bus fleet.
“I hope the state government, the city council and others will take this into account in traffic planning and pedestrian routes, particularly at pedestrian crossings,” he said.
Rapid Penang began operating 15 electric buses today, comprising 14 measuring 8.25 metres and one measuring 12 metres.

The electric buses are equipped with an Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System that produces external warning sounds to help pedestrians and other road users detect their presence, particularly at low speeds.
The buses also have an Advanced Driver Assistance System that provides driving assistance and warnings to bus captains.
Loke said the transition involved more than introducing vehicles with new technology.
“Operational readiness, charging facilities, maintenance and workforce capabilities must be strengthened alongside implementation,” he said.
Rapid Penang is scheduled to receive a total of 75 electric buses by March 2027 under the first procurement phase, which also includes 175 buses for Rapid KL.
017428da3022e648: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for concrete, collective action by Asean member states, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Brunei, to tackle transboundary haze that continues to threaten millions of people across the region.

Its president, Dr L. Sivanesan, said countries must enforce the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution by setting clear implementation deadlines, ensuring compliance and publicly reporting progress.
"Regional agreements must deliver results rather than remain promises on paper," he said in a statement today.
Sivanesan said authorities should also investigate and prosecute those responsible for illegal burning, including companies linked to Malaysia.
"Penalties must be imposed to deter repeat offences, while concession maps and fire hotspot data should be made publicly accessible," he said.

He said haze should also be treated as a public health emergency, with authorities activating emergency health response plans, monitoring haze-related illnesses and ensuring healthcare facilities had sufficient staff, medicines and equipment.

Vulnerable communities should be protected through appropriate respiratory protection, including free face masks for those who can use them safely and clean-air shelters in badly affected areas, with priority given to high-risk groups.
Sivanesan also called for consistent school closure procedures based on air quality levels, alongside support for students from low-income families during home-based learning.
He said authorities must prevent fires through investment in peatland restoration, fire prevention measures, early warning systems and sustainable alternatives to slash-and-burn practices.
"These preventive efforts must be carried out throughout the year," he said.
Doctors could treat the health effects of haze, but tackling its root causes required firm action and sustained commitment from governments across the region, he added.
Sivanesan said Southeast Asians should not have to accept toxic air as a recurring annual problem after more than two decades of haze episodes.
"Clean air is a basic right, not a privilege. After more than two decades of recurring haze, people deserve tangible results," he said.
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution was signed in 2002, committing member states to work together to prevent, monitor and fight fires.
275cc8cd880e6010: KUALA LUMPUR: Electricity supply to several areas in Johor Baru was fully restored within 77 minutes after a fire broke out at the Kangkar Tebrau Main Intake Substation yesterday, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) said.
The affected areas included Bandar Dato Onn, Taman Daya, Kempas, Bandar Ulu Tiram, Desa Tebrau and Johor Jaya.
In a statement today, TNB said its technical teams were mobilised immediately to restore power in stages.
"Two TNB technical personnel who were at the site during the incident sustained injuries and are receiving further medical treatment at Sultan Ismail Hospital in Johor Baru.
"Both are reported to be in stable condition," it said, adding the families of the injured personnel had been informed and were with them.
TNB said the cause of the fire remains under detailed investigation by its technical team, as well as the Fire and Rescue Department.
The utility added it would extend its full cooperation to ensure a thorough investigation into the incident.

"TNB apologises for any inconvenience caused by the electricity supply disruption. TNB also extends its appreciation and thanks to all affected customers for their patience and cooperation throughout the restoration process."
0be1e2779da21ab3: PETALING JAYA: The government should use Malaysia’s trade leverage to hold plantation companies linked to forest fires in Indonesia accountable for the recurring transboundary haze, says Bersama’s Lee Chean Chung.

The former Petaling Jaya MP said Malaysian-linked plantation companies operating in Indonesia should be required to disclose their concession maps and fire records through Bursa Malaysia and the plantation and commodities ministry.
In a statement, Lee also proposed barring companies linked to fires from government procurement, certification and incentives, as well as publicly naming them.
“Malaysian capital must not profit from smoke that poisons Malaysian lungs,” he said in a statement.
Lee also called on the government to introduce a Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, saying the proposed legislation had remained unimplemented since he first called for it in August 2019.

He said the law should allow the environment department to compel companies to provide information and enable prosecution and civil claims against Malaysian and foreign firms responsible for haze affecting Malaysia, regardless of where the fires occurred.
Lee also proposed allowing satellite data and plantation concession maps to be used as evidence, alongside requiring companies to prove that their land was not the source of fires.

He urged Malaysia to activate existing Asean mechanisms to address the haze, including formally raising concerns over Indonesia’s obligations under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution.

Lee also called for an extraordinary meeting of the agreement’s Conference of the Parties, a meeting of the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee involving Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, and greater use of the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control.
Lee said the issue should also be raised at the 49th Asean Summit in Manila from Nov 16 to 18, with Malaysia seeking firm commitments from regional leaders and regular progress reports.
He criticised Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s stance that Putrajaya had done its best to tackle the transboundary haze affecting Malaysia, arguing that diplomatic engagement alone was insufficient.

He also questioned the foreign ministry’s handling of allegations involving Malaysian companies linked to fires in Indonesia, citing a recent parliamentary statement that the natural resources ministry had yet to receive confirmation from Wisma Putra on the companies concerned.
Lee said satellite hotspot data, concession maps and ownership records were available, and argued that the main obstacle was a lack of political will rather than a shortage of evidence.
“The haze is not a natural disaster. It is man-made, preventable and recurring,” he said.
A total of 24 areas in the country recorded unhealthy API readings at noon today, down from 27 yesterday afternoon.
Yesterday, government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil said most of the fires observed in Indonesia occurred outside oil palm concessions owned by Malaysian companies.
On Monday, foreign minister Mohamad Hasan said Southeast Asian foreign ministers would discuss how to tackle haze blanketing parts of the region ahead of the Asean summit next month.
ace9b2123194f0ea: SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has reminded the public that freedom comes with responsibility and called for social media users to engage with respect and courtesy.

Sultan Ibrahim, who is also Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Chancellor, said this in response to the misuse of social media by certain quarters to incite others, spread hatred and sow division in society.

“Do not turn social media into a platform to insult, swear at, vilify or humiliate others. Differences of opinion are no reason for hostility. We may disagree, but we must express our views in respectful and courteous language.
“If you wish to criticise, do so constructively. If you wish to correct someone, do so with tact and consideration,” His Majesty said.
Sultan Ibrahim was speaking at the 105th UiTM Convocation Ceremony at the Tuanku Canselor Grand Hall, UiTM Shah Alam, here today.
Also present was Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who is also UiTM Pro-Chancellor.
Sultan Ibrahim also called on the public not to misuse artificial intelligence (AI) technology to create fake images and videos with the intention of insulting or embarrassing others.
His Majesty said that behind every name and face subjected to hatred and insults was a person with a family, dignity and feelings.

“From a young age, we are taught to respect our elders, speak with decorum, and not look down on others on the basis of religion or race, because good manners are not merely about politeness, but are the lifeblood of the nation’s dignity.
“However, amid today’s advances in digital technology and social media, some have forgotten their manners and feel free to insult, abuse, verbally attack and humiliate others,” His Majesty said.
In this regard, Sultan Ibrahim urged the public not to readily believe or share any news without first verifying its authenticity.
“Do not let our haste to be the first to share unverified information turn us into people who spread slander and hatred.

“I want to see us become a mature society in our communication, free to express ourselves with courtesy, bold enough to share our views without insulting others, and firm in defending our convictions without sowing hatred,” His Majesty said.

At the ceremony, Sultan Ibrahim also consented to the UiTM campus in Jalan Othman, Petaling Jaya, being renamed the Tun Arshad Ayub Campus in recognition of his services and contributions to spearheading the establishment and development of UiTM since 1965.

The late Arshad, who died in 2022, was the first director of the MARA Institute of Technology (ITM) from 1967 to 1975. The institution, now known as UiTM, regarded him as a pioneer who laid the groundwork for its educational development.

His Majesty also congratulated all graduates, parents and the university community on their achievements, expressing hope that UiTM would continue to progress in producing successful graduates for the nation’s progress.

The convocation ceremony, which was also attended by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir and UiTM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin, will see a total of 32,630 graduates receive diplomas and degrees in various fields from today until December 16.
UiTM also conferred the title of Professor Emeritus on Datuk Dr Roziah Mohd Janor, its first female former vice-chancellor. — Bernama
867b00bca8b1b8d1: BANGKOK: The International Monetary Fund projects that Japan's nominal gross domestic product, measured in US dollars, will be overtaken by India and Britain in 2027, falling from fourth to sixth place globally, Kyodo News reported.
Since 2023, Japan has ranked fourth behind the US, China and Germany.
The IMF's GDP projections were released earlier this month, amid the yen's continuing weakness against the US dollar and sluggish Japanese economic growth.
According to the IMF's World Economic Outlook, Japan's nominal GDP is projected at US$4.3419 trillion in 2026 and US$4.4676 trillion in 2027.
For both years, the calculations appear to have been based on an exchange rate in the range of 158 yen to the dollar.
Meanwhile, India's GDP is expected to reach US$4.5211 trillion in 2027, jumping from sixth to fourth place globally.
In the key quarterly report released in April, the IMF had projected that Britain would overtake Japan in 2029. However, it is now forecasting British GDP at US$4.4889 trillion in 2027.
While Japan's real economic growth is projected at 0.7% in both 2026 and 2027, India's economy is expected to expand 7% on a fiscal year basis in both years.
The report said that “India remains among the fastest-growing major economies,” driven by “resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.”
The report said Britain's economy is likely to grow 1.3% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027.
Japan had long held the No. 2 spot globally, but following China's rapid growth, it fell to third place in 2010 and was overtaken by Germany in 2023, slipping to fourth place.
1c536db509260bfd: TOKYO, Oct 17 — Japan’s weather agency withdrew an erroneous alert for a magnitude 9.9 earthquake minutes after issuing it, apologising for the warning that disrupted transport.

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) had initially warned yesterday that a magnitude 9.9 earthquake occurred near the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Chishima Islands, setting off loud emergency alerts on millions of mobile phones.
The JMA clarified later that a 6.9-magnitude quake occurred near Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula at a depth of 160 kilometres (100 miles) just after midday.
“We deeply apologise for the significant inconvenience and concern caused to the public,” JMA official Shinya Tsukada told reporters.
The alert did not cause widespread panic, but briefly disrupted public transport.
According to the JMA, the error stemmed from an anomaly in calculating the earthquake’s epicentre.
The estimated magnitude was based on an incorrect assumption that the epicentre was about 680 kilometres farther from Japan than it actually was, the weather agency said.
Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive 9.0-magnitude undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.
A 9.9-magnitude tremor would have released about 22 times as much energy as the 2011 quake, according to local media. — AFP
1b6d5e666e7fe050: KOTA BARU: Twelve years after Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 vanished, Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) benefits continue to provide financial stability to next-of-kin who lost their primary breadwinners.

The Dependants' Benefit (FOT) under the Employment Injury Scheme of the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) provides continuous financial security to affected families, helping dependants cover basic household expenses and fund tertiary education.
One recipient, Nurlaila Ngah, 52, said she was left to raise three school-going children alone after her husband, flight steward Wan Swaid Wan Ismail, went missing in the March 8, 2014 incident.

"I am grateful my husband contributed to Perkeso while serving as a flight steward with Malaysia Airlines since 1995. Even though he has not been found, his children receive Perkeso benefits as the incident was categorised as an employment injury.
"We have received more than RM2,500 a month through this benefit since 2014, supporting us in managing daily expenses," she said.
Nurlaila, who resides in Nilai, Negri Sembilan, said her children, aged 20, 22, and 24, continue to receive monthly assistance while pursuing higher education under conditions set by Perkeso.

"Social security protection plays a vital role when a family member suffers a workplace misfortune. At the very least, it eases the family's burden, especially when children pursue higher education," she added.
Similarly, Norazlinda Ayub, 51, wife of missing flight steward Junaidi Mohd Kassim, said her monthly benefit of over RM2,700 helps cover educational expenses for her two children, aged 20 and 23.

"After losing my husband, I had to stay strong and rebuild my life for the children. I work in the unit trust industry, where income depends entirely on my own efforts," said Norazlinda, who lives in Shah Alam, Selangor.

She added that her husband had contributed to Perkeso since joining the airline around 1997, and urged self-employed workers to contribute under Perkeso's Self-Employment Social Security Scheme (Lindung Kendiri).
"We may feel financially capable today, but we never know what tomorrow brings," she said.
Perkeso deputy chief executive (operations) Azirruan Arifin said 50,945 active dependants were receiving the FOT benefit under Act 4 as of Aug 31, 2026.

He said assistance includes periodic benefit payments at a daily rate equivalent to 90 per cent of the worker's assumed average daily wage, subject to a minimum of RM30 and a maximum of RM178.50 per day.
Azirruan added that eligible dependent children can access education loans, while the scheme also provides a one-off funeral benefit of up to RM3,000.S

d8c31347156c78ff: KUALA LUMPUR: Agrobank mempergiat program memburu ikan asing bertujuan memulihara spesies ikan tempatan di Tasik Ampang Hilir demi keseimbangan ekosistem air tawar.
Presiden merangkap Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Agrobank, Tengku Ahmad Badli Shah Raja Hussin, berkata kelestarian alam sekitar penting bagi memastikan kelangsungan sektor agromakanan negara.
“Kelestarian sektor agromakanan bukan hanya bergantung kepada pembiayaan dan pembangunan industri, tetapi juga kepada kesihatan alam sekitar yang menyokongnya.

Program itu melibatkan sekitar 250 peserta daripada tujuh agensi dan organisasi, termasuk 43 warga kerja bahagian pembangunan Agrobank.
Antara aktiviti utama ialah menangkap ikan asing menggunakan pukat, jala, pancing, dan bubu yang disediakan Jabatan Perikanan.

Kepentingan usaha itu turut digambarkan menerusi rekod Jabatan Perikanan yang menunjukkan 146 daripada 154 ikan direkodkan di Tasik Ampang Hilir, atau 94.8%, merupakan spesies asing. Hanya lapan ikan direkodkan terdiri spesies tempatan, termasuk ketutu, haruan, puyu, dan kaloi.

Program tanggungjawab sosial korporat (CSR) itu turut disertai Kementerian Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam (NRES), Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL), Aquaria KLCC, TCE Tackles, dan Persatuan Pemancing Semalaysia.
Sementara itu, Ketua Setiausaha Kementerian Pertanian dan Keterjaminan Makanan, Isham Ishak, mengalu-alukan sokongan Agrobank menerusi inisiatif CSR bagi menjayakan program tersebut.
Beliau berkata, penglibatan sektor korporat membuktikan usaha memelihara alam sekitar boleh diperkukuh melalui kerjasama antara kerajaan, sektor swasta dan masyarakat.

“Saya berharap kerjasama strategik seperti ini dapat diteruskan dan diperluas kepada lebih banyak inisiatif yang menyokong pengurusan sumber perikanan secara mampan serta pemuliharaan biodiversiti negara,” katanya.

Ketua Pegawai Pembangunan Agrobank, Ahmad Ariff Abu Bakar, berkata program itu antara lebih 30 aktiviti dijalankan Jabatan Perikanan bagi membantu memulihkan keseimbangan populasi ikan tempatan dan asing di tasik serta sungai negara.
Beliau berkata, usaha itu penting bagi meningkatkan kesedaran mengenai keperluan memulihara spesies ikan tempatan, terutama di Tasik Ampang Hilir yang mempunyai populasi ikan asing yang tinggi.
332ace56465116ae: GEORGE TOWN: The final report on the Long Lellang helicopter crash is expected to be published within a year, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.

d8b9d8f995949ce9: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — Rapid Penang began operating its first 15 electric buses today, marking the start of its transition towards an electric bus fleet, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke today.

“There will be new buses arriving every month to complete Rapid Penang’s fleet of 75 buses by March next year,” he told a press conference after launching the service at the Rapid Penang Depot in Weld Quay here.
He said the initial fleet comprises 14 buses measuring 8.25 metres and one measuring 12 metres.
“The shorter buses make it easier to travel, particularly on the island, where they can enter narrower roads and more densely populated areas,” he said.
Loke linked the rollout to Penang’s efforts to reduce carbon emissions.
“This is part of the public transport sector’s contribution towards a more environmentally friendly state,” he said.
According to a statement issued by Rapid Bus, the first procurement phase involved 250 electric buses across Rapid Penang and Rapid KL, with 175 allocated to the latter.
At the press conference, Loke clarified that the estimated RM200 million investment covered all 250 buses under this phase.
The procurement is divided into two delivery stages to coordinate the arrival of buses with charging infrastructure readiness and depot requirements.
Under the first stage, Loke said Rapid Penang would receive 40 buses and Rapid KL 110.
Deliveries began in June and are scheduled to be completed by December 31.
He said the second stage involved another 35 buses for Penang and 65 for Rapid KL, with deliveries expected to begin in January and finish by March 2027.
